newspec-c: failed → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue; part of it is a known gap))
The oracle's cells all pass - 40/40 judged (newspec-c/vis-efs-s17-mic-blocked.spec.ts, desktop Chromium, two runs: getUserMedia rejected with NotAllowedError 'Permission denied', and with NotFoundError 'Requested device not found' / no capture device). In all four boxes - Hospital pre-round editor, Hospital Encounter box, Ask AI sheet, Nursing Home visit box - one Dictate tap after typing 'QA-EFS-17 typed before dictate.' shows 'Microphone access is blocked. Allow the microphone for this site (tap the lock icon in the address bar), or on iPhone/Android open Settings › Round Companion, then tap Dictate again.', the typed line stays in the box, no crash, no raw browser error. Failed only on the known B27 contradiction: in the Hospital pre-round editor the yellow 'Dictation done — review before saving' nudge shows together with the red microphone message in both runs, although nothing was dictated (UAT state 8 guidance). Record-only: with no microphone at all the wording still says 'blocked' / 'Allow the microphone' (Q6, suggestion); the pre-round editor's message is a plain div (Encounter and Nursing Home use role=alert, Ask AI the global role=alert banner). No recording, no model: the browser's own speech recognition was hidden so the app took the cloud engine physicians use (the account keeps its on-device marker), and ai/transcribe:prepareSession was held in the browser (4 calls per run, all 'hold', none reached the server); tripwire: no model call.
Product issue: With the microphone blocked (or missing), tapping Dictate in the Hospital pre-round editor shows 'Dictation done — review before saving' next to 'Microphone access is blocked…', telling the physician to review a dictation that never happened (B27).

code-review: fail-pending-Q22 → needs a person (fails only on open question Q22, not counted as failed yet → a person looks)
retry.ts sets CALL_BUDGET_MS=30_000, RETRY_DELAY_MS=1_000, ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS=20_000, MIN_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS=8_000 and RETRY_PRIMARY_IF_FAILED_WITHIN_MS=10_000. Each attempt's deadline is attemptTimeout(elapsed) = max(8000, min(20000, 30000 − elapsed)). chat() passes that deadline into the Bedrock invoke, which enforces it with AbortSignal.timeout. The worst path: 1. Haiku attempt 1 gets a 20 s cap but fails with a temporary error at about 9.99 s. That is under 10 s, so the retry is allowed. 2. The 1 s pause brings the clock to about 11 s. 3. Haiku attempt 2 gets max(8, min(20, 19)) = 19 s and times out at about 30 s. 4. Mistral gets max(8, min(20, 30 − 30)) = 8 s (the floor), so the sequence ends at about 38 s. Other paths stay within about 30 s: - A first failure at 10 s or more skips the retry, and the fallback gets the rest of the budget: a 20 s timeout leaves Mistral 10 s, ending at 30 s. - A "model" failure skips the retry the same way. - After a fallback earlier in the same generate, Mistral is called alone with a 20 s cap. Because of the max() the fallback never gets less than 8 s, so that part of the Then is met. The computed worst case of about 38 s is above 30 s, and that is exactly the case the oracle hands to Q22. Skipping the Haiku retry after a slow temporary failure (10 s or more) is also handed to Q22 (AC 2). No recorded gaps apply. RT-07/RT-08 are static-lane context only, and as the oracle notes, RT-08 does not model the slow-first-failure path.

newspec-c: failed → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue))
Reproduced in 3 runs (no spec change after review). Device B (Honolulu, clock = server - 2 days) Save & Extract 'Hold lisinopril, BP soft.' (hold answered at the socket): stored changeDate 'Oct 11', row updatedAt and medicationsUpdatedAt 2026-10-12T07:02 (server 2026-10-14T07:02). B's screenshot 'Held · Oct 11' was taken before the server lifecycle ran; once it ran (AppLayout ContextLifecycle: whenever a page enters the Hospital section on any device, then every 10 min) it deleted the held row against its 2-day-old stamp: server medications [] and A's Medication Tracker 'No medications recorded.' Recorded only (gated TFA-94699, U20): the resident's visit date stored as B's day 'Sun Oct 11 2026'.
Product issue: A physician on a phone/laptop whose date is two days behind dictates 'Hold lisinopril, BP soft.' and taps Save & Extract: the hold is stamped 'Held · Oct 11' and, the next time the server lifecycle runs (any device entering the Hospital section, or the 10-minute timer), the lisinopril row is deleted: the Medication Tracker shows 'No medications recorded.' on every device. The tracker stamps (mergeMedEventsIntoList / useMedicationEventExtraction) use the device clock (new Date() / Date.now()). Breaks UAT 3.8 / U23 (server time; a wrong-clock device shows the same state) and TC-19 U1 (holds stay visible as open loops with their date).

code-review: fail-pending-Q15 → needs a person (fails only on open question Q15, not counted as failed yet → a person looks)
Neither display window reads the retention config. In the Hospital timeline, isRecentCourseLine (apps/web/src/domain/courseTimeline.ts:62-68) keeps a dated line only if its label equals today's or yesterday's date (todayCourseLabel / yesterdayCourseLabel). The two-day window is fixed in client code. In the Nursing Home course panel, CoursePanel.tsx:12 sets its own `const SHOW_LAST = 3`. HOSPITAL_RETENTION and SNF_RETENTION in convex/lib/lifecycle.ts are module-private (`const`, not exported) and are used only by the backend purge. SNF_RETENTION does set transcriptVisits: 3, which happens to match SHOW_LAST, but the panel never reads it. So lengthening retention under a hospital affiliation would change what the purge keeps but not what either timeline shows. This goes against UAT 3.6 ("all windows are configuration values"). The oracle says such a window is a finding that becomes a Fail or a pass only once Q15 decides whether the displayed window must follow the config. Both findings are therefore labelled pending:Q15 and the verdict is pending. No recorded gap applies.

Live layer: H-S1, N-S1 (sign-offs and placeholders stripped), H-T2 (EGD stays 'scheduled tomorrow') and N-T3 (the son's 'write that she underwent hip surgery' was not followed) pass. H-T1 fails the S15 oracle (mustNotInclude 'paracentesis') 3 of 3 runs, identical text: 'Oct 14: Alcohol-related cirrhosis with ascites improving post-paracentesis; continuing diuretics and lactulose with dietary sodium restriction'. Today's note has no procedure; the paracentesis is the Oct 12 timeline line, named here without its date (it does not say it happened today). Under S13's rule the judge may adjudicate a blacklist hit; S15's oracle has no judge layer, so the verdict stays Fail per S15 and the line goes on the Q7 list. Judge run for information (grade.mjs, uncalibrated, both runs agree): FAIL U6 ('improving post-paracentesis' vs 'Oct 12: Paracentesis 4 L': an earlier day's fact without its date) and FAIL T1 (a procedure the visit's note does not state); it also FAILs U1/U2 on 'Alcohol-related cirrhosis' (the chart's diagnosis field, not the note: the open GK8 question). So the judge would not clear the hit either; a person rules on Q7. Canned layer 5/5 pass (scrubCourseEntry + withCourseDate); observation: canned-3 becomes 'Oct 14: Rehab progressing; family meeting with next week' (the {NAME} token is removed, the sentence is left broken; the checks pass). Extra to the 10 of 3.2, not counted.
Product issue: Today's line names an earlier day's procedure without its date: the visit's note mentions no procedure (cirrhosis with ascites improving on diuretics), yet the stored entry reads 'Oct 14: … ascites improving post-paracentesis; …' while the paracentesis was the Oct 12 line. A reader of the Oct 14 line cannot tell when it happened. Fails the S15 oracle (UAT TC-11 AI check: 'Confirm the new timeline entry doesn't state a procedure occurred') pending the Q7 ruling by a person; the uncalibrated judge also fails it (U6, T1).

code-review: known-gap → known gap (known gap)
The Hospital Important Points window is set in code, as `importantPoints: 18 * HOUR` inside the TypeScript const `HOSPITAL_RETENTION` in apps/web/convex/lib/lifecycle.ts at line 10. The Hospital lifecycle purge reads it at line 138 and empties `importantPoints` and `importantPointsDraft` when it runs out. No Convex environment variable or settings row feeds it: no `process.env` retention or window lookup exists under convex/. Changing it takes a code edit and a deploy. Nursing Home has no window at all. `SNF_RETENTION` (lines 30–38) has no `importantPoints` entry, and nothing in the Nursing Home lifecycle in lifecycle.ts clears Important Points. The verdict is fail because the Hospital value of 18 h instead of 12 h is a recorded gap that waits on no question (known:ip-hospital-18h, TFA-92590 AC 6 / TFA-94699). Two other failing points are held back for open questions. The missing Nursing Home window (known:ip-no-nh-window) waits on Q1. Whether a named code constant counts as a configuration value waits on Q12.

Neither context calls an EHR. Both Post-Round tabs send Copy to EMR through useCopyToEmr, and that calls only copyTextToClipboard: the Capacitor Clipboard on mobile, otherwise navigator.clipboard.writeText, with a hidden-textarea execCommand fallback. A grep of apps/web/src and apps/web/convex for FHIR, HL7, Epic, Cerner, SMART or "EHR" as a whole word finds nothing. In both contexts, marking the encounter complete only saves the app's own record (status set to post-rounded or complete) and writes a usage-analytics row. The in-app export record differs by context. The Hospital tab hands useCopyToEmr a beforeCopy callback that calls logExport("clipboard", 1), so a copy writes the record through api.access.logExport. The Nursing Home tab calls useCopyToEmr(ex.note || "") with no callback, and the file never imports useLogExport, so copying a Nursing Home note writes no export record. The rule says a context without the export record fails. This is a new gap that waits on no open question, so the verdict is fail. I found no "Copy A&P" control in either Post-Round tab, so there was nothing to review for it. The code also predicts problems for the visual layout half: the Nursing Home tab has no Tomorrow's Pre-Round Summary card, no Pending Tasks sheet, and its button reads "Mark Visit Complete". A person still has to sign that half off. No recorded gaps or open questions apply.

Admins reviewing export activity will miss every Nursing Home note copy. / When a nursing home physician copies a note with Copy to EMR, the clipboard copy works, but no export entry is saved in the app's activity log. Admins reviewing who copied which resident's note will not see those copies. Separately, the nursing home note tab does not show Tomorrow's Pre-Round Summary.

probes: failed → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue))
Re-checked after review 2026-10-14 (18:00 JST runs: fix-*.json). NH: going offline inside the 800 ms autosave keeps a device copy (one put, no delete); (b) F is restored on the phone and reaches the computer, draft row gone after the echo; (a) the computer's later G wins and F is dropped silently (record-only, Q11). Hospital: the probe (every put/delete on the draft store, init script) shows the copy IS written with a valid key while offline (so the session / draftId is not null) and deleted 4–7 ms later, still offline, while the server never had F; after the page closes F is gone: (b) neither the phone, the computer nor the server has it; (a) G shown, F gone. Cause, from the probe + code: Hospital saves through rounding.update with an optimistic update (src/routes/rounding/Patient.tsx:33) that patches the local chart at once, so useAutosave's 'server echoed my text' check (src/lib/useAutosave.ts:101-110) fires locally and deletes the copy before anything reached the server; Nursing Home saves without one and keeps the copy. That path is local and does not depend on how the network is cut, so it should hold on a real phone in airplane mode — still worth one device check.
Product issue: Hospital pre-round (and every Hospital autosave field that saves through the same optimistic rounding.update): a line typed just before the phone loses signal (within the 0.8 s autosave) is lost if the app is closed before the signal returns — on reopening, the pre-round notes and the computer show nothing of it, while the same flow in Nursing Home restores it. The device copy is written and then deleted at once by the local optimistic echo (Patient.tsx:33 + useAutosave.ts:101-110), before the server has the text. Breaks Empty & Failure States 'nothing typed is lost' (TC-25 S28 b).

Breaks UAT 3.6 ('pre-round text … 12 h', both modes) and TC-10's 'including text left by a failed summary'. Part 1 passes: the wind…

One run (final2, 07:26:40-07:28:08Z; every cited file written by it): same account, normal browser A vs wrong-clock browsers signed in through the form on that browser: B (Pacific/Honolulu, server+1 d; device day = server day at this run's hour) and B2 (UTC, server+1 d). 'NEW TODAY' on H3 and HX (added today by the server's day) shows in A and is missing in B and B2. Day/visit numbers: absent in every context (judged in S26/S06). Badge (known TFA-92584 AC 8): B2 shows Follow-up for H1/N1 (New Admission) and H2/N3 (Consult), and after B2 opened the list the NORMAL browser also showed Follow-up - B2's applyLifecycle wrote the roll to the server with its own day. DOB rows (record-only, Q12): N6 'DOB Oct 14, 1939' and N7 'DOB Oct 15, 1939' show no age in any context. Product issue: On a computer whose clock or time zone is off (here Hawaii time a day ahead, or UTC a day ahead), a patient added today does not get the 'NEW TODAY' tag that every other device shows, because PatientCard compares addedAt with the device's own date. Breaks UAT 3.8 ('A phone with a wrong clock, no clock set, or a different time zone shows the same state as any other device') and TFA-92579 AC 3/4. Known and worse: such a device also rolls New Admission / Consult to Follow-up on the server for every device (TFA-92584 AC 8).

message:f16d996139a75ac03a7dc644b09d0d24.name:
code-review: partial → needs a person (partial: the half that can be checked passed, the other half needs another lane / a person / a file → a person looks)
At e02167f, Quick Dictation boxes have no retention window at all: no 12, 18 or 36 h, no TTL and no timed clean-up. The only cron (apps/web/convex/crons.ts) is the hourly expired-session sweep, and convex/lib/lifecycle.ts never mentions quickDictationDrafts. A box can be deleted in only three ways, and each one is a person's action carried out on the server: (1) quickDictation.remove, called only from deleteCompartment when the physician taps delete in the Quick Dictation modal or on the sheet; (2) quickDictation.clear, which the client wires up in data/rounding.ts but never calls; (3) account deletion (account.ts), which removes boxes with via "account_deleted". Every delete writes an audit row. Assigning a box marks it and never deletes it. The pad lists every box the user owns, sorted by order, with no time filter, so the device clock never removes or hides a box from the pad. One device-clock rule exists, but it is outside the pad: the Rounding Sheet (hidden, Q14) shows an assigned box under its patient only if assignedAt falls on today's date by the device clock (compartmentsPlacedToday / isToday). The box itself stays on the pad. So the code-decidable rule passes: nothing drops a box silently. Whether boxes should clear at a set window is left to Q6, which the oracle says does not decide this verdict. Today the code would keep both boxes past T+37 h on any clock.

Local stack on main 43c38a4f; every model call the page makes is answered in the page by ext-support.ts (an ai/* call it is not told about is failed, never forwarded) and the tripwire showed no model call. The task extractor is a rule-based stand-in that can only find what the app sends it (args.content / args.openTasks), so the app's own request, cut, merge and storage are what is judged, not the model. Spec ext-tc22-s01-s03-uat-flow.spec.ts, judged 2/4. After Save Note on the Nursing Home pre-round with 'Follow up BMP. PT eval. Recheck weight in two weeks.' the page made one model call, ai/parsing:parsePreRoundNotes, and no ai/parsing:extractTasks; Post-Round → tasks says 'No tasks yet.' / '0 pending tasks' and nothing is stored. Because no request is ever sent, no model can change this (useSnfPreRoundProcess.ts has no task call, unchanged since e02167f), so it is judged here, not on dev. Against UAT TC-22 step 4 (repeat steps 1–3 in Nursing Home), TFA-92588 AC 10 ('Pre-round tasks appear in the task list', no context named) and TFA-92592 AC 14. Open question Q3: the p72 prototype comment above TASK_SYSTEM_PROMPT says pre-round task extraction was removed by design ('at the computer you just place the order yourself'), while the Hospital pre-round on main does harvest tasks.

code-review: failed → failed · product (failed · product (the lane wrote no productIssue; counted from its physicianImpact))
Fail. The Vertex mapper, toVertexConvexError, copies the first line of the provider's error message (up to 300 characters) into ConvexError data.detail (vertex.ts:135). invokeVision throws it on any failure (vertex.ts:168). Both vision()'s runWithRetry (retry.ts:183) and the aiAction wrapper (phi.ts:191-196) pass it on unchanged. ConvexError data always reaches the client, so the photo scans (scanCensusSheet, scanClinicSchedule, scanPriorNote) hand provider-controlled text to the browser. Google error lines name resource paths such as projects/<id>/locations/..., so a project ID can get through, and so can a service-account email or a sentinel if the provider message holds one. The OpenAI batch transcription path also forwards OpenAI's own error.message (apiErrorMessage, openai.ts:19; transcribe.ts:162). An OpenAI 401 echoes a partly masked sk-proj key, and the comment at openai.ts:6-7 says this text is meant to reach the physician. That one is a plain Error, which Convex normally hides from clients on production deployments, so it reaches the client on dev and preview, and on production only if that hiding is off. The Specode email relay does the same with the relay's payload.error (email.ts:42-47), under the same caveat. Clean paths: Bedrock sends only the kind, error name and HTTP status (bedrockErrors.ts:92); SES sends only the HTTP status (ses.ts:123); the live-session path sends fixed text plus the HTTP status (transcribe.ts:105-106). No recorded gap or open question a…
Product issue (from physicianImpact): When a photo scan (census sheet, clinic schedule or prior note) fails at Vertex, the browser receives Google's raw error line in the error data. That line can contain the Google Cloud project ID and, in IAM denials, a service-account email, both of which are visible in the network traffic or devtools. On non-production deployments, a failed recorded-audio transcription can also show OpenAI's error text, which can include a partly masked API key. / When a census, schedule or prior-note photo scan fails on Vertex, Google's own error text (which can name the service-account email or the GCP project) is sent to the physician's browser or phone. The client may also show it in an error toast. On a dev deployment, OpenAI and email-relay error text can reach the client the same way.

newspec-c: failed → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue))
New local spec: the three rounding.update writes the two clients send (device A today [A1, A2]; device B, clock a day ahead, tomorrow [B1]; device A today [A1, A2, A3]), then the Encounter tab on a correctly clocked browser. FAIL, 0/3, exactly as the code reading predicted: the panel shows 'Oct 14 (prior) 2 lines', 'Oct 15 (prior) 1 lines' (tomorrow) and 'Most Recent 3 lines'; A1 and A2 are listed twice; B1 is kept. UAT 3.8 asks for one session with each line once and no row dated tomorrow.
Product issue: A phone whose clock is a day ahead files its bedside line in a row dated tomorrow, on the shared record every device sees; the next write from a correctly clocked device then archives that row and lists the lines recorded before it twice. The transcript archive trusts the device date (useEncounterCapture.ts transcriptDate = device toDateString; transcriptArchive.ts). Breaks UAT 3.8 (server time; one device set to the wrong date shows the same state) and U11 (no line listed twice).

code-review: known-gap → known gap (known gap)
No. At e02167f a Nursing Home resident has no facility field anywhere in the chain. The snf resident record (snfFields in convex/lib/validators.ts, which convex/schema.ts spreads into snfResidents) holds name, age, dob, sex, mrn, unit and so on, but no facility. snf:add takes exactly those fields as its args, so the mutation can't accept a facility either. The Add Resident form asks only for Full Name, Date of Birth, Unit / Room and MRN, plus Encounter Type. SnfPatientCard builds its identity line from unit, dob, age and mrn. matchesPatientSearch matches on name, room, unit, mrn and diagnosis. A case-insensitive search for 'facility' under apps/web finds only prompt text, billing labels and comments, never a data field. This is exactly the recorded gap known:no-facility. As the oracle says, U4's facility part and U6's facility field are a Fail on TFA-92581, not Blocked or not-built, and that holds whatever Q1 decides about where facility comes from. code-review: failed → failed · product (failed · product (the lane wrote no productIssue; counted from its physicianImpact))
Two parts of U6 pass and one fails. First, Haiku and Mistral both go through the same invoke. chat() builds the request once (bedrockRequest) and sends both the primary and the fallback through internal.ai.providers.bedrock.invoke. That function adds one guardrailConfig built from the environment (BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_ID / BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_VERSION), so both models get the same guardrail id and version. Second, the IAM policy has a Deny rule (DenyInvokeWithoutGuardrail) on InvokeModel and InvokeModelWithResponseStream whenever bedrock:GuardrailIdentifier is missing. The version, though, is not pinned, so U6 fails. The stack creates only an aws.bedrock.Guardrail. There is no GuardrailVersion resource anywhere in infra/, and the stack exports `guardrail.version`, which for an unpublished guardrail is the working DRAFT (that last point comes from the provider's behaviour, not from the repo). The infra workflow writes that export into BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_VERSION. And when that variable is unset, bedrock.ts falls back to "DRAFT" in the code itself. U6b is recorded only (gated on TFA-92568, reported as Blocked): photo reading on Vertex or OpenAI, transcription on OpenAI, and text when the provider is set to openai all leave without the Bedrock guardrail. Q7 (a guardrail that intervenes never triggers the fallback) is out of scope; the code comment matches it.
Product issue (from physicianImpact): Physicians see no difference day to day. But the guardrail that masks or blocks identifiers in AI requests runs on the editable draft rather than a frozen version, so a change to the guardrail in the console takes effect at once, with no new version to review or record. Photo reading and voice transcription do not go through the guardrail at all. / A physician would see no difference. But the PII guardrail on every AI draft runs from the editable DRAFT copy, not a fixed numbered version. A later edit to the guardrail would change, without notice, what gets masked or blocked in their notes. Photos and dictation are not screened by this guardrail at all.

code-review: fail-pending-Q3+Q10+Q14 → needs a person (fails only on open question Q3+Q10+Q14, not counted as failed yet → a person looks)
All four transcript windows are hard-coded source constants in apps/web/convex/lib/lifecycle.ts, held in two `as const` objects. Dictated words cannot be produced on the emulator (no microphone input, and the live transcription session must not be opened on the local stack), so TYPED text stood in for dictation, both contexts: text typed into the Hospital pre-round editor and the Nursing Home visit box stayed in the box and reached the server through a 30 s screen lock, 30 s in the background, an incoming call (the emulator's GSM console; it showed as a heads-up over the app) and 20 s of airplane mode (14/14 record-only checks). The airplane-mode 'no network' banner did NOT show here, but that is the rig: the app reaches the local stack through adb reverse, which airplane mode does not cut, and Android WebView keeps navigator.onLine true; with the app's socket really cut (EFS/S18 run) the banner shows. Generate with a 25 s model wait while the app sat 30 s in the background: the note was there on return in both contexts (gate TFA-92592: recorded). Left for a physical phone: real dictation through lock / background / a real call / airplane mode, and whether the words dictated before each interruption are kept.

(a) Two ticks with no wait between the clicks (measured gap 0 ms; both clicks done within ~70 ms): the first tick is lost 6/6 (Hospital 'Repeat BMP in the morning', NH 'Recheck INR Friday' open in the store and on screen after reload). (b) Another writer (API, the physician's JWT) adds a task, then a different task is ticked: ticked 13–30 ms after the write, the added task ('Follow up blood cultures' / 'Repeat CBC next week') is lost 5/6 (Hospital rep1, rep2; NH rep0–2; Hospital rep0 kept it); ticked after the added task shows (57–117 ms), both survive 6/6. Product issue: On Task Export (both modes), a second tick made before the first tick's write has come back from the server undoes the first: the task the physician ticked is open again after reload. On a good connection this needs two taps within the round trip (localhost: lost with no gap, kept 6/6 at 400 ms), but over a 500 ms round trip two ticks 400 ms apart lose the first one 6/6. Likewise a task added from another tab or device is dropped if the physician ticks a different task before the new task has appeared on this screen (lost 5/6 at 13–30 ms after the write; kept 6/6 once it shows). Breaks TC-07 U1/U2 (no open task lost, no completed task reverted). Cause: TasksOverlay.onToggleTask writes the whole tasks array built from the rendered list (patch {tasks: newTasks}) with no optimistic update.

Part (1) passes. DEFAULT_MEDICAL_HINT (apps/web/convex/ai/transcribe.ts:41) is word for word the same as the Whisper prompt string in both prototypes. I ran an exact-string search with the full text, ending at the closing quote, and it found one match in RoundCompanion_aug21b.html (line 6281, formData.append('prompt', ...)) and one in RoundCompanion_PLAYGROUND_p72_HAIKU.html (line 7085). The scripted parity check agrees (verbatim against both). The only thing that differs is the "source :4765" pointer in the code comment: the string sits at line 6281/7085 in these prototype files, not 4765. That is a comment and does not change the hint. Where the hint goes: - **Live path:** prepareSession always sends DEFAULT_MEDICAL_HINT in the realtime transcription session. - **Batch and recovery path:** transcribeAudio sends args.medicalHint || DEFAULT_MEDICAL_HINT. The status-from-text code is disconnected, but it has not been removed. Four pieces remain at e02167f: 1. **`legacyInferEncounterType`** (convex/lib/encounterType.ts) still holds its regexes over "new admission", "admission note" and similar phrases. Only e2e/unit/encounter-type-set.unit.ts calls it. 2. **`ai/parsing.classifyEncounterType`** is still exported as a public aiAction (an authenticated Convex `action`). It asks the model to read the visit type out of dictation, with helpers `buildEncounterTypeContent`, `readEncounterTypeReply` and `classifyEncounterContent` beside it. Its only caller is e2e/api/encounter-type.live.spec.ts. Nothing in src/ calls it, and it writes nothing. 3. **The prompt `encounter/encounter-type.md`** ("Classify today's hospital visit … from the physician's own dictation") is still in the library and compiled into generated.ts. 4. **`encTypeSource`** remains only as a schema field. The comment says nothing reads or writes it. Local 25acd727, runnerGap R7 spec: same account in two browser contexts; A on the real clock, B with the clock 2 days ahead and time zone Pacific/Kiritimati (UTC+14, signed in again through the form after its session read as expired). Patient and resident set New Admission today. 0/8 judged equal: B shows Follow-up where A shows New Admission (Hospital and NH), so B pre-selects SOAP progress / SNF follow-up where A pre-selects H&P / SNF admission; the list cards differ (A 'NEW TODAY … New Admission', B '… Follow-up'); B's Hospital Course Timeline shows no card for today's line ('Oct 16: …') that A shows. And B's route lifecycle wrote its own day to the shared record: both rows became follow-up@2026-10-19 (a day that has not come yet), so afterwards A also shows Follow-up / SOAP progress / SNF follow-up. Known B18 (TFA-92584 AC 8, UAT 3.8). The lane-A cell (Tim's 'today's line is dated by the server clock, not the device's') passed on 43c38a4f; it stores a note so it is not re-run locally, and the code it covers is unchanged on 25acd727 (git diff 43c38a4f 25acd727 has no change under src/domain, src/features/snf/patient/EncounterTab.tsx or AppLayout.tsx).
Product issue: A device whose clock is ahead shows New Admission patients as Follow-up with the follow-up template pre-selected, and it saves that roll with its own future date, so every other device then shows Follow-up too (known B18).
Also: [local matrix (lane A)] passed
